### 🟢 Approval recommended The one-function change reuses a verified pure helper, correctly handles every traced edge case, only tightens an internal loopback check, and is backed by thorough unit tests. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR This PR fixes a classification bug in `isLoopbackHost` (`packages/server/src/bind-host.js`). Previously, IPv4-mapped IPv6 hosts were classified as loopback by naive string prefix matching (`::ffff:127.` / `::ffff:7f`), which incorrectly matched non-loopback addresses like `::ffff:7f:1` (which is actually `0.127.0.1`) and the incomplete `::ffff:7f`. The fix reuses the existing `mappedV6ToV4` helper from `ssrf-guard.js` to parse the full embedded IPv4 address and only treats it as loopback when it falls in `127.0.0.0/8`. This tightens an internal host-locality check that feeds the non-loopback bind warning and related callers, so it is a small, security-positive correction. **Changes:** - Replace prefix-matching of IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback with a full parse via `mappedV6ToV4`, correctly rejecting `::ffff:7f:1` and `::ffff:7f`. - Add focused unit tests pinning hex/dotted tails, case-insensitivity, first-hextet boundaries (`7e00`/`8000`), extra hextets, and malformed dotted tails, with documented proof-of-red. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | packages/​server/​src/​bind-host.js | Parses the IPv4-mapped IPv6 tail with `mappedV6ToV4` and checks for `127.` instead of prefix matching. | | packages/​server/​tests/​bind-host.test.js | Adds tests covering hex/dotted forms, case, hextet boundaries, and malformed inputs. |
Review effort: Balanced
